intake.problem: Build a new Spring Boot-style URL shortener web service exposing a fixed HTTP contract: POST /api/shorten to create or retrieve a short code for an absolute http/https URL (returning 201/200 with JSON {code, url}, deduplicating identical URLs to the same code, and returning 400 for invalid schemes, malformed URLs, or missing url field); GET /{code} to redirect (301/302) to the original URL or 404 if unknown; GET /api/stats/{code} to return click counts as JSON or 404 if unknown; a hand-rolled per-IP rate limiter capping POST /api/shorten at 30 requests/second returning 429 on excess; persistence of URL mappings and click counts in an embedded H2 database; and a working actuator health endpoint at /actuator/health.
assumptions: This is a new standalone service (no existing codebase to integrate with)
Framework is Spring Boot (implied by 'actuator' health endpoint)
H2 can run in-memory or file-based mode; either satisfies 'embedded H2'
Short code generation algorithm (e.g., base62 of an auto-increment ID or random string) is an implementation detail left to the engineer
Short code length/charset is unconstrained by the spec, so any reasonable scheme is acceptable
Rate limiter state can be in-memory (per-instance), single-node deployment assumed — no distributed rate-limiting requirement
Click counting only counts successful GET /{code} redirects, not GET /api/stats calls
URL validation for 'malformed URL' means standard URI/URL parsing failure, not stricter DNS/reachability checks
No authentication/authorization is required on any endpoint
No expiration/TTL for shortened URLs is required
JSON error body format for 400/404/429 is unspecified in detail; a simple {"error": "message"} shape is acceptable
Existing/duplicate detection is by exact URL string match (not normalized, e.g. trailing slash or query param order differences)
ambiguities: What short code format/length/charset is required (numeric, base62, fixed length, custom alphabet)?
Should redirect use 301 (permanent, cacheable) or 302 (temporary) — spec allows either, but this affects client caching behavior and must be picked deterministically
Should POST /api/shorten return 200 vs 201 specifically when the URL already exists, or is either acceptable at the implementer's discretion?
What exact JSON shape/fields should error bodies for 400/404/429 use?
Is URL normalization required before dedup comparison (e.g., trailing slashes, case-insensitive host, default ports), or is exact string match sufficient?
Does the rate limiter need to be distributed/shared across instances, or is single-instance in-memory limiting acceptable (implies no horizontal scaling)?
What HTTP client IP extraction strategy should be used behind proxies (X-Forwarded-For vs remote address) for rate limiting?
Should short codes ever expire or be deletable, or is persistence permanent?
Is there a maximum URL length or additional validation rules (e.g., blocking localhost/internal IPs for SSRF protection)?
Should the H2 database be file-based (persisted across restarts) or in-memory (reset on restart)?

concerns: The REQUIRES_NEW wrapping in createNew() runs each insert attempt in its own transaction, but this changes commit visibility semantics: if the outer request-level @Transactional method rolls back after createNew() succeeds (e.g., due to a later exception in the same service call), the inner REQUIRES_NEW insert has already committed independently, leaving an orphaned/committed UrlMapping row that is inconsistent with the outer transaction's rollback — this violates the design's stated goal of '@Transactional to guarantee consistency between read-check and write'.

The design explicitly says 'all wrapped in @Transactional boundaries' as the mechanism for read-check/write consistency; introducing a manual TransactionTemplate with PROPAGATION_REQUIRES_NEW inside the service is an architectural deviation not mentioned in the design and not called out as an approved change — this should be flagged/documented as a deliberate contract exception rather than silently introduced.

Using saveAndFlush inside a REQUIRES_NEW transaction means the dedup check (in shorten()) and createNew()'s insert are no longer part of the same transaction as before; a concurrent duplicate insert between the dedup lookup and the createNew() call is only guarded by the DataIntegrityViolationException retry loop, which is fine, but the surrounding outer transaction no longer sees the new row as part of its own atomic unit — if the outer transaction later fails and rolls back, the committed inner insert becomes a permanent orphan with no compensating action.

The ShortenControllerWebTest change replaces the Spring-managed, properly configured TestRestTemplate bean with `new TestRestTemplate(new HttpClientOption[0])`, which loses any context-customizer configuration (base URL, message converters, auth) that Spring Boot normally injects; the comment asserts the autowired bean 'does not reliably disable redirects,' which contradicts documented Spring Boot behavior (TestRestTemplate with @SpringBootTest and default RANDOM_PORT should already not follow redirects by default) — this suggests a test observed a flaky/incorrect symptom and worked around it without root-causing it, which is risky for future maintainers.

No repository/migration change is shown for the unique constraint on original_url or code enforcing DataIntegrityViolationException — this diff's correctness assumption (that races are caught via DataIntegrityViolationException) hinges on schema constraints not shown in this diff; if those constraints were altered or are missing, the whole retry-on-conflict logic silently breaks.
